answer: Raman is worth testing in the lab first for glucose in this broth, but the broth's fluorescence may mask the Raman signal, so its background must be measured before relying on Raman. The 0.1 g/L accuracy cannot be guaranteed before a calibration is built and validated on your own samples, and the order cannot be approved until the fiber and routing are confirmed. One Raman probe is not supported for glucose, ethanol and biomass together.

inline.headline: Test Raman in the lab first, after a fluorescence background check, with NIR as the comparison
inline.probe: Raman fiber probe (excitation wavelength to be fixed after the fluorescence check)
inline.install: at the fermenter probe port, location to be confirmed
inline.fiber: silica fiber (existing 80 m silica fiber, Vis-NIR type to be confirmed)
inline.not_final_because: Fluorescence may mask the Raman signal in this broth, no accuracy is possible before own-sample calibration, and the fiber type and routing are unknown.

problems.text: The broth's strong autofluorescence can hide the Raman signal, because Raman is weak and fluorescence is often much stronger. Measure the broth's fluorescence under the planned laser before relying on Raman; NIR is the robust online comparison.

No accuracy can be promised before calibration. A 0.1 g/L accuracy depends on a calibration model built and validated on your own samples, and which method works cannot always be predicted in advance.
Approval is asked before the facts allow it. Approval needs the fiber type, link length, routing and conditions; these are not supplied, and method choice depends on them.

One Raman probe for glucose, ethanol and biomass together is not supported by the sources. Raman is cited for glucose, acetate and lactate, while biomass is tracked by UV-Vis turbidity or by NIR combined with fluorescence.

methods.why: Gives direct detection of glucose in aqueous media, but only after the fluorescence background is shown to be low enough.
Robust online fiber method; tracks glucose and ethanol at major-component levels but may lack sensitivity below 0.1 %.
Intrinsic fluorophores are sensitive; NIR combined with fluorescence gave more accurate biomass in yeast fermentation.
Suited to liquids, but mid-IR absorption limits it to thin layers and water absorbs IR more strongly than Raman.

questions.q: What is the fluorescence background of the broth at your planned excitation wavelength, or can you measure it?
questions.why: This decides whether Raman can be used at all in this broth.

questions.q: What is the exact fiber type of the existing 80 m silica fiber, including coating or jacket, and how is it routed?
questions.why: Approval needs the fiber family, jacket and routing, and the fiber must transmit the method's range.

questions.q: What concentration ranges must be measured for glucose, ethanol and biomass, and which independent laboratory method will provide the reference values?
questions.why: Accuracy and detection needs can only be judged against a known range and an independent reference.

questions.q: Is the broth heterogeneous (live cells, solids, gas bubbles) so that the probes may not see the same spot?
questions.why: If it is, a combined same-spot probe is needed instead of separate probes.

questions.q: Do you have any existing spectra of the broth, and how many batches and samples are available for calibration?
questions.why: Spectra show whether the method sees the difference and how many samples a model needs.

experiment.objective: Show whether Raman sees glucose, ethanol and biomass in this broth despite its fluorescence, and whether a fused NIR and Raman model beats the best single method on the same data.
steps: Measure the broth's fluorescence background at the planned excitation wavelength before relying on Raman.
Collect Raman and NIR spectra of broth samples across the fermentation, time-synchronised.
Measure glucose, ethanol and biomass on the same samples by an independent laboratory analysis.
Build one chemometric model per analyte per method, validate on held-out batches, and compare Raman, NIR and fused NIR+Raman on the same validation data.
Check that the fiber transmits the Raman range used (silica Vis-NIR 350-2400 nm) before any approval.
experiment.go_no_go: criteria come from the client (the 0.1 g/L target is the client's own)

pathway.key_features: Raman bands for glucose and ethanol and NIR ethanol windows at 1.5-2.2 um must be identified in the broth; none are yet known for this sample.
pathway.path_reason: Key spectral features and a validated calibration do not yet exist, and the fiber and fluorescence facts are missing.

multispectral.why: NIR sees polar groups and Raman sees the molecular backbone, so their information is complementary; NIR + Raman gave the best results for pellet coating.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused NIR + Raman PLS model with the best single method on the same held-out batches, and keep the combination only if it wins; if the broth proves heterogeneous, switch to a combined same-spot probe.
